title: Choose the visual world for the Clayface report
question: The roll assigned Card Back Stat Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Card Back Stat Line
options.lineage: Trading-card backs: team bands, the season stat line and the fine-print stats credit
options.thesis: Each island is a collectible card, and the report is its back, where the stat line lives.
options.viewport: A navy shell bar with section tabs; two island cards side by side, key art as the front strip and the stat line underneath (fights, clays, reached 20, redeemed), the redemption rate stamped largest.
options.risk: Collectible styling tips into toy-like if bands and foil are used beyond the stat line.

raised.raise: Every figure carries a catalog number (S1 to S10) pointing to the source file it came from.
Hierarchy by scale alone: the redemption rate at display size, labels at caption size, nothing bolded in between.
Havoc yellow is reserved for the headline figure and for what can be clicked; nothing else takes it.
One geometry, the banded card, frames key art, stat lines and charts alike.

options.label: Broadcast Head-to-Head
options.lineage: Esports broadcast stat packages: lower thirds and head-to-head bars
options.thesis: HH3 and HH2 face off like two teams on a tournament broadcast.
options.viewport: A studio-blue shell; one head-to-head panel where each metric is a split bar, HH3 from the left and HH2 from the right, the winner's value lit.
options.risk: Familiar: dark broadcast graphics sit close to the dark-dashboard default many runs land on.

options.label: Coupon Book
options.thesis: Each island's weekend is a coupon book: one coupon per clay-system step, stamped when verified.
options.viewport: Two coupon rows, one per island, each coupon a funnel step with carbon numerals; a VERIFIED stamp on checked figures and VOID on what was not measured.
options.case: Fuses well: stamped states make verification visible at a glance; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Travel ephemera has no link to Havoc Hotel or Fortnite.

options.label: Twin Columns
options.lineage: Reference editions set around a centre rail of keys
options.thesis: HH3 and HH2 twinned in two columns around a centre rail of metric names, sources in the margin.
options.viewport: HH3 figures in the left column, HH2 in the right, metric keys down a vermilion centre rail, each source noted in the outer margin.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the centre rail is a natural HH3-vs-HH2 comparison; loses on audience identification.
options.risk: Reads like a scholarly edition, far from Fortnite.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The report as a specimen sheet driven by one slider.
options.viewport: One giant figure with a slider that morphs the grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a client reading results has nothing to slide.
options.risk: Pure typography with no tie to the game.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Friendly cards with one action colour.
options.viewport: A single column of rounded cards and a bottom bar.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as the generic look the client should not see.
options.kept: One saturated colour reserved for actions.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every artifact numbered, data drawn as a pulse of white lines.
options.viewport: A black field with a stacked pulse plot of daily dwell.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels hurt clarity for a client.
options.kept: Every figure numbered back to its source.

options.label: Guide Map
options.thesis: Rooms as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: One green lobe per island with capsule labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful map styling reads childish to the client.
options.kept: One geometry drives layout, art and state.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean product-analytics dashboard, executed at the best tools' level.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, a row of KPI tiles, two charts and a sortable table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any analytics template by design.
